## Model selection (pre-registered rule; decay test amended)

A model wins only if it (1) reproduces the observables, masses and decays: no rejection at α = 0.05 after Holm's correction over its four Pearson χ² tests, and (2) is physically sound: non-degenerate, basis converged, radial nodes = radial quantum number, m_b − m_c in the heavy-quark window, √b in 0.44 ± 0.04 GeV (lattice), 1P centre of gravity − h at the PDG value, ⟨v²⟩ < 0.5; each within 2σ. Among those, the lowest AIC = χ²_masses + χ²_decays + 2p. The rule and its thresholds were fixed before the final sweeps (docs/EXPLANATION.md). Amendment, made after the results were seen: the registered decay test is linear in Γ with a theory error ∝ Γ_NLO, so its pull is bounded below by −1/f and it cannot reject an overprediction. Gate 1 now requires both the registered linear test and the same test on ln(Γ_PDG/Γ_NLO) (log; symmetric, milder on underpredictions), each with Holm over its four tests: the amendment only adds rejections. Ranking and tiebreak: the registered AIC (linear decays). Verdicts: linear = the rule as registered (2 pass), log = log form alone (2 pass), both = the amended rule.

## Goodness of fit: masses (Pearson χ² at the declared error)

Every model refitted with the declared theory error of the masses, c c̄ 13.30 MeV and b b̄ 3.87 MeV: the Paule–Mandel random-effects estimator (Paule and Mandel 1982) pooled over the physical set, so one error budget for all models, favouring none. χ²/ν and its p-value P(χ²_ν ≥ χ²) are the conventional test. ## Goodness of fit: decays (held-out benchmark)

The measured annihilation widths of the fitted states, predicted by the mass-only fit at the declared error (the fit graded above), which never saw them: Pearson χ² with V = V_exp + V_theory + V_par. Theory error: the truncation of the α_s series by scale variation (μ = M/4 … M, half the band, correlated within a process) in quadrature with the O(v²) relativistic correction of NRQCD power counting, ⟨v²⟩Γ. ppp: the Bayesian posterior predictive p-value of the same widths (stats sweep), linear form. log: the amended form (the selection requires both), on ln(Γ_PDG/Γ_NLO) with the same errors taken relative (scale band correlated within a one-loop-factor class; parametric error diagonal), symmetric in over- and underprediction; z: the standardised log ratio of the worst width (z > 0: the model is too small).

## Bayesian inference: the theory floor marginalised

Posterior of the parameters and of σ_th (flat priors in u, i.e. in ln θ for positive parameters; flat in ln σ_th, scale invariant), Gaussian likelihood with its normalisation; 4 Metropolis chains. Posterior predictive p-values (Gelman, Meng and Stern 1996) for T = χ² and T = max|z|: small means the data are more discrepant than the model's own replicas. With σ_th marginalised the χ² check is not sensitive to the overall scale; max|z| flags single states.

## Diagnostic: the truncation estimate (A/B, non-relativistic kinetic energy)

Not a grade (the grades above use standard methods); a physics diagnostic. σ_a is the part of the first omitted term, −⟨p⁴⟩(1/8m₁³ + 1/8m₂³), that the model's parameters cannot absorb (the model's own values shifted by the term and refitted; σ_a solves the floor equation for the unabsorbed residuals R). At σ_a, χ²/ν is the conventional test. λ: (PDG − model) = λR, 1 if the omitted term is the misfit, 0 if unrelated. Darwin, orbit-orbit and 1/m potential terms are of the same order and also omitted, so σ_a estimates one term of the truncation, not all of it. Per model, σ_a is a self-consistency check, not a ranking: a less flexible model absorbs less of the term and passes more easily.

## Diagnostic: each model's own floor (physical set)

σ_th: the Paule–Mandel estimator per model (χ² = N − p); its interval is the Q-profile interval (Viechtbauer 2007), the χ² test inverted. χ²_PDG: Cochran's Q, PDG errors only, at the floor fit and refitted (σ_th = 0). The largest p-value over the set is 10^-33: no model reaches the precision of the data. σ_th: the χ² test of 'the model is accurate to σ_th' inverted (every σ_th it accepts at 68 % / 95 % CL). Shift: largest parameter change of the PDG-only refit, in units of the floor fit's error. t: standardised LOO miss, every term of its error from the refit without the state.

### Does one accuracy scale describe both flavours?

Floor of state i = κ·u_i with u = 1 (uniform), ⟨v²⟩_i, or ⟨p⁴⟩_i/8m³ (the first kinetic term the non-relativistic Hamiltonian omits), from each model's own fit. κ solved per system; under one κ for both, F = (χ²_c/ν_c)/(χ²_b/ν_b) ~ F(ν_c, ν_b). With ν_c = 4 the test is weak: at 95 % it accepts κ_c/κ_b within about 0.33–2.2, so it rejects a wrong flavour scaling by a factor ≳ 3 but cannot tell ⟨v²⟩ from ⟨p⁴⟩/8m³.

| p4 | 19 | 0.97 | 0.54 | 0 |
